subject: Request: Temporary APAC warm-standby RTO/RPO variance during customer migration
messages:

Cc: FinTrust Procurement <procurement@fintrust.com>, Ravi Singh <ravi.singh@fintrust.com>

Subject: Request: temporary RTO/RPO variance for APAC warm-standby (May 18-22)

Hi Naomi,

We have a planned data migration and schema transition scheduled in APAC over the weekend of May 18-20 (extended window through May 22 for cutover validation). Our migration runbook requires a maintenance window during which we cannot guarantee the usual client-side warm-standby performance.

Specifically, we need a formal exception for the following temporary SLA change in the APAC warm-standby region for the dates 2028-05-18 00:00 through 2028-05-22 23:59 (local time):

- RTO: up to 3 hours (from standard 60 minutes)
- RPO: up to 60 minutes (from standard 15 minutes)

We understand this is outside Redwood's default commitments and are prepared to accept mitigations outlined in our migration plan attached (fintrust-migration-plan.pdf). Procurement is looped in for documentation. Please reply with what Redwood would need (runbooks, on-call, credits, or timelines) to approve and execute this temporary variance.

Thanks,
Karen Liu
Director, Platform Operations
FinTrust

From FinTrust (what you already supplied / what we still need):
- Full migration runbook + rollback criteria (received).
- Confirmation of traffic cutover start/end times and expected QPS.
- Primary on-call contacts for the migration weekend.

From Redwood (what we propose):
- Temporary SLA variance for APAC warm‑standby: RTO 3h / RPO 60m for 2028-05-18 00:00 through 2028-05-22 23:59, subject to conditions below.
- Mitigations: extended monitoring, pre-warmed caches, prefix KV priming, and an enhanced escalation path to our SREs in APAC and EU.
- Runbook checklist and a short action plan (I asked Aditya to draft the implementation steps and risks).
- Commercial: standard exception fee/credit framework — we'll propose a capped credit if the variance is exercised. Jonas, can you weigh in on commercial?

I'll collate a single exception addendum draft and a short operational checklist we need signed by procurement. I cc'd Marissa to coordinate the runbook rehearsal and war-room coverage.

—Naomi

Subject: Re: Request: temporary RTO/RPO variance for APAC warm-standby (May 18-22) — technical impact and mitigations

Team / Karen,

I reviewed FinTrust's migration plan and ran a short simulation against our APAC warm‑standby topology. Summary: feasible with the following technical controls and lead time:

- Pre-warm KV and prefix cache: 48h lead time to prime popular prefixes (we'll need a list of critical prefixes).
- Traffic shaping & throttles: Implement a 4x short-term per-customer throttle for heavy background jobs during the cutover — 6–8 hours of engineering config change.
- Cross‑region spillover to EU: routable but will add 250–400ms tail latency for affected requests; requires a firewall rule change + DNS TTL drop 24h prior, estimated 4–6 hours ops work.
- Monitoring & automated failover: enable extra SLO alerting channels and an active war-room dashboard; ~2 hours to provision and ~2 engineers on-call during the window.

Risks:
- If the migration introduces schema mismatch that corrupts cache priming, RPO guarantees may be invalidated — we need clear rollback criteria and an agreed throttling policy.
- Cross-region spillover increases unit latency and could impact customer UX; this is a last-resort mitigation.

I attached a short action plan (redwood-action-plan.docx) with step-by-step tasks, owners, and a backout checklist. If procurement/agreement looks good, we can finalize times and rehearsals.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Senior Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Exception addendum: APAC warm-standby RTO/RPO variance (proposal and next steps)

Karen — thanks for your patience. Below is Redwood's proposed exception addendum and operational requirements for the APAC window. This is a formal offer pending procurement signature and a brief runbook rehearsal.

Exception (proposed)
- Window: 2028-05-18 00:00 to 2028-05-22 23:59 (APAC local time)
- Temporary SLA commitments for APAC warm-standby during the window: RTO up to 3 hours; RPO up to 60 minutes.
- Commercial cap: if an SLA breach attributable to Redwood occurs during the exception window, FinTrust will be eligible for a one-time credit not to exceed 10% of the monthly committed spend for the affected billing period.

Conditions
1) Runbook rehearsal: one 60–90 minute dry run with FinTrust and Redwood SREs before 2028-05-16.
2) Pre-warm actions: FinTrust provides critical prefixes list by 2028-05-14; Redwood completes cache priming by 2028-05-16.
3) War-room coverage: Redwood will provide two SREs in APAC and one EU backup during the window; FinTrust to provide primary contacts.
4) Cross-region spillover: permitted only as a last‑resort mitigation and with explicit prior consent from FinTrust.
5) Rollback criteria: agreed in runbook; mutual signoff required before automatic rollback.
6) Documentation: procurement signs the exception addendum (DocuSign link below).

Next steps and timeline
- Action: Procurement to review and sign addendum -> DocuSign: https://docusign.com/FinTrust-SLA-Exception-FT-2379
- Action: FinTrust to provide prefixes and final cutover schedule by 2028-05-14.
- Action: Schedule runbook rehearsal week of 2028-05-15 (Marissa to coordinate).
